result.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: in lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve contains 'Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})' — a synchronous in-process call to the entire feed poll (which opens and parses SiteSetting.feed_polling_url, per poll_feed.rb's 'rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)'), executed inside the RetrieveTopic Sidekiq worker. This is a real performance/throughput risk grounded in specific code, but it is not a correctness defect — behavior is still correct, just potentially slow and blocking. That makes it a substantive non-bug architecture concern.

judged_text: perform_retrieve runs the entire feed poll synchronously via Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inside the Sidekiq worker instead of enqueuing it, so a worker retrieving one embed URL blocks on opening and parsing the whole remote feed plus readability fetches. A slow/hung feed_polling_url stalls the Sidekiq worker for the full HTTP timeout on every first-time embed hit, degrading all background job throughput for sites with embedding enabled.

adjudication.rationale: Verified: `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously (lib/topic_retriever.rb) when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, rather than enqueuing a scheduled/async job. Since `TopicRetriever` is invoked from the Sidekiq job `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb), this can block that worker while `PollFeed#poll_feed` performs `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and parses the feed (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). This is a throughput/architecture/performance concern grounded in the diff, not a functional correctness defect.
